messages:
Priya: Heads-up — NovaPay signed a 3-month enterprise commit PO. They want a guaranteed baseline for checkout chat and an ability to absorb spikes during promos. Target peak: 1,000 QPS chat, avg tokens in 200 / out 300 (500 total). Embeddings 10% of calls. Start date: May 6. Need: recommended reserved GPUs, autoscale policy, preheat plan, and short security FAQ for procurement.

Ben: Nice. A few clarifying Qs: are peaks sustained (minutes) or instantaneous (seconds)? expected p95 output length? model family preference (13B quant / 30B float / 70B)?

Priya: They say peak is sustained ~3-7 minutes for promo bursts, typical valley ~120 QPS. Model preference: prefer a 30B quantized for quality but will accept 13B quant if cost constrained. Want fallback plan if latency or costs spike.

Rob: Quick ballpark math:
```
peak_qps = 1000
avg_tokens = 500
tokens_per_sec = 1000 * 500 = 500_000 tps
assume_13B_quant = 50_000 tps per GPU
assume_30B_quant = 28_000 tps per GPU
gpus_13B = ceil(500_000/50_000) = 10
gpus_30B = ceil(500_000/28_000) = 18
```
So 13B quant -> ~10 GPUs, 30B quant -> ~18 GPUs. Add 1-2 GPUs for headroom + canary slots.

Maya: Operational recommendations: reserve a monthly commit of 10 GPUs (13B quant) as baseline. Buy burst credits to allow autoscale up to 14 GPUs (scale_step=1 GPU). If customer insists on 30B quality at peak, call that out as a separate "high-quality" scenario with a larger commit or higher burst spend.

Priya: How do we handle warm cache / KV for checkout flows? They have many returning sessions per promo.

Rob: Suggest persistent KV caching + preheat top 200 prefixes and warmup heavy customers 6 hours before promo window. That typically improves decode-side load by ~25% on hot sessions. Also set `batching.max_tokens=4096` for embeddings path and aggressive short-batch for chat.

Ben: Autoscale policy I recommend:
- metric: tokens/sec per pool + pending queue length
- min_reserved = 6 (keep baseline cheap capacity)
- commit = 10 GPUs
- burst_limit = 4 GPUs (autoscales to 14)
- cooldown = 120s
- prewarm_slots = 1 dedicated slot for canary/QA
Route priority: reserved pool -> burst pool -> graceful throttle with 503 when queue length > 200 to protect SLOs.

Maya: Also include a fallback model chain: primary 30B-quant, fallback 13B-quant (faster) for latency-triggered fallback. Do not fall back to much smaller model for payment UX — risk of hallucination.

Priya: Pricing ask from the customer: what's monthly delta between reserved and burst? need quick numbers for procurement.

Rob: Tentative internal numbers: reserved_gpu_monthly ~= "$6k per GPU" (13B-equivalent), burst_on_demand ~= "1.7x reserved". So for commit=10 GPUs reserved -> ~$60k/mo baseline; bursting 4 GPUs on-demand ~+ $40k/mo if used continuously (prorated). Prewarm slot cost = ~reserved hourly rate * hours. Flagging finance to confirm exact pricing and any enterprise discounts.

Priya: Security procurement checklist items they care about: EU data residency, SOC2, BAA, KMS integration (CMK), audit log retention, penetration test report.

Maya: Short answers we can give in procurement packet: 1) EU region deployed for customer data (we can host in eu-west-1). 2) SOC2 Type II report available on request. 3) We can support customer-managed keys in Private or VPC setups; Hosted can use envelope encryption with customer key options on Private. 4) Audit logs retained 90 days by default; extended retention available as add-on. 5) BAAs possible — legal review required.

Ben: Note: HSM-backed KMS for encryption-in-use requires Private deployment and networking changes; call out expected lead time 2-4 weeks.

Rob: Reliability guardrails: health checks on p50/p95/p99, error-rate alarms, and a queued throttling policy at 800ms p95 to prevent overload. Canary rollout suggestion: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 48-72 hours with automated rollback on error spike or latency > 1.25x for > 5 minutes.

infra-bot: scheduler: preheat-job created for 2024-05-05T22:00Z (warm top-200 prefixes, duration 6h).

Priya: Action items:
- Rob: detailed sizing slide + sensitivity table (13B vs 30B vs token length) — due EOD tomorrow
- Maya: ops runbook + preheat checklist + canary steps — draft by tomorrow 10:00am PT
- Ben: pricing ballpark + finance ask — email finance and share numbers by EOD
- legal-bot: start BAA intake; estimate timeline and required docs

legal-bot: intake-ack: BAA request logged, typical turnaround 5-12 business days depending on countersign.

Priya: Thanks team. I'll attach the one-pager to the SOW and loop in the customer. Please tag me if you need extra info from NovaPay (we have contact who can share token length histogram). :pray:
